info.title: Registrum API
info.description:
# Registrum API

UK company intelligence - structured financials, director networks, and intelligent caching - from a single developer-friendly REST API.

---

## Quick Start

### 1. Get your API key

Sign up to receive your API key.

### 2. Authenticate your requests

Include your API key in the **`X-API-Key`** header with every request:

```
X-API-Key: reg_live_your_key_here
```

> **Using the interactive docs below?** Click the green **Authorize** button at the top of this page, paste your API key, and click **Authorize**. All subsequent "Try it out" requests will include it automatically.

### 3. Make your first request

Search for a company:
```
GET /v1/search?q=tesco
```

Get an enriched company profile:
```
GET /v1/company/00445790
```

### Client libraries & examples

- **Python**: [companies-house-api-python-starter](https://github.com/RegistrumUK/companies-house-api-python-starter) - auth, rate-limit backoff, pagination, and the iXBRL-vs-PDF gotcha, in one file
- **Node.js**: [companies-house-api-node-starter](https://github.com/RegistrumUK/companies-house-api-node-starter) - same, using the built-in `fetch`
- **MCP (Claude, Cursor)**: [registrum-mcp](https://github.com/vdmeu/registrum-mcp) server, with a [prompt cookbook and example scripts](https://github.com/RegistrumUK/registrum-mcp-examples)

---

## How It Works

This API sits on top of the [Companies House public API](https://developer.company-information.service.gov.uk/) and adds:

- **Intelligent caching** - responses are cached so repeat queries are instant and you never hit rate limits
- **Enriched profiles** - company age, accounts status, size classification, and more in a single call
- **Director networks** - discover all companies connected through shared directors
- **Structured financials** - parsed iXBRL filings returned as clean JSON with current + prior year

## Upstream Call Costs & Throughput

Each endpoint makes a different number of calls to the Companies House API on your behalf.
**Cached responses cost nothing** - once a company is fetched, repeat requests within the cache window are instant.

| Endpoint | Upstream calls (cold cache) | Cache duration |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/search` | 1 per unique query | 1 hour |
| `GET /v1/company/{n}` | 1 per company | 30 days |
| `GET /v1/company/{n}/directors` | ~N+2 (N = number of directors) | 30 days |
| `GET /v1/company/{n}/network?depth=1` | ~N+2 | 30 days |
| `GET /v1/company/{n}/network?depth=2` | 50–200 (capped at 30 connected companies) | 30 days |
| `GET /v1/company/{n}/financials` | 2–3 (filing history + doc metadata + iXBRL download) | 90 days |
| `GET /v1/health` | 0 | - |
| `GET /v1/health/deep` | 1 | - |
| `GET /v1/health/probes` | 0 | - |

**Safe throughput on cold cache (approximate, across all customers):**
- Search and company profiles: up to ~100 unique queries per minute
- Directors and network (depth=1): up to ~8 different companies per minute
- Network (depth=2): up to ~2–3 different companies per 5 minutes

If these rates are exceeded, responses slow briefly (typically 5–15 seconds) while upstream capacity
recovers - you won't receive errors, just slightly higher latency. The cache eliminates this concern
for any company queried more than once within the cache window.

## Response Format

Every endpoint returns responses in this standard format:

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": { ... },
  "cached": true,
  "cache_age_seconds": 3421,
  "credits_used": 1,
  "credits_remaining": 487
}
```

## Response Headers

Every response includes:
- `X-Request-Id` - unique ID for this request (useful for debugging/support)
- `X-API-Version` - current API version
- `X-Data-Stale: true` - only present when serving expired cache during an upstream outage

## Rate Limits

Every new key gets full access for its first 60 days - no monthly quota, every endpoint - then moves to Free. Live values: `GET /v1/plans`.

| Tier | Price | Calls/month | Calls/day | Burst |
|------|-------|-------------|-----------|-------|
| Free | Free | 50 | 15 | 10/min |
| Web | £9/mo | 500 | 50 | 30/min |
| Pro | £49/mo | 4,000 | 400 | 100/min |
| Enterprise | On request | Unlimited | Unlimited | 150/min |

**Pro/Enterprise-only features:** `network?depth=2`, PSC chain traversal, and ECCTA compliance monitoring.
Free/Web requests to these return `403 PLAN_REQUIRED` with an `upgrade_url`.

## Errors

Errors return a JSON object with `status: "error"` and a human-readable `detail` message:

```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "detail": "Company 99999999 not found",
  "request_id": "a1b2c3d4-..."
}
```

| Status Code | Meaning |
|-------------|---------|
| 400 | Invalid input (e.g., bad company number format) |
| 401 | Missing or invalid API key |
| 404 | Company not found |
| 422 | Validation error (e.g., search query too long) |
| 429 | Rate limit exceeded |
| 502 | Companies House API is temporarily unavailable |
| 500 | Unexpected server error |

## Usage Dashboard

Track your API calls, quota, and reset date at **[registrum.co.uk/dashboard](https://registrum.co.uk/dashboard)**.
Sign in with the email you used to get your key - no password needed.

Or call `GET /v1/usage` (free, no credit consumed) to read quota programmatically.

## Need Help?

Include the `X-Request-Id` from your response headers when contacting support - it helps us trace exactly what happened.

get.description:
Check if the API server is running.

Returns 200 with uptime and version info. No authentication required.
Use this endpoint for uptime monitoring (e.g., UptimeRobot, Better Uptime).

**Upstream usage:** 0 - no upstream calls made. Safe to poll at any frequency.

200.description: Successful Response

get.description:
Check that all upstream dependencies are reachable.

Tests connectivity to the Companies House API and Supabase database,
and reports per-dependency status and response times. No authentication required.

Also reports **`api_self_check`** - not an upstream, but this API's own
self-check probe: whether it is still running here, and what it last saw
when it called `GET /v1/company/{n}` through the public hostname. An
external uptime monitor watching this endpoint for the word `unhealthy`
therefore also catches the case where our internal monitoring has stopped.

- **healthy** - all dependencies responding normally
- **degraded** - one or more dependencies are slow or unreachable (the API will still serve cached data)

**Upstream usage:** 1 upstream call to the Companies House API (a lightweight search probe).
Do not poll this endpoint at high frequency - once per minute is sufficient for monitoring.

200.description: Successful Response

get.description:
Return the latest result from each background health probe.

Probes run automatically on a schedule. The headline ones:

- **api_self_check** (every 5m) - calls `GET /v1/company/{reference}` on the
  public hostname, with a real API key, and requires all three of: HTTP 200,
  the right company in the body, and a response inside a 5-second budget.
  This is the only probe that asks the customer's own question. A 200 alone
  is not a pass: during the 2026-08-13 outage `/v1/health` answered 200 at
  12-15 seconds while ~90% of real traffic was 499/502.

- **event_loop_lag** (every 60s) - measures how long the API's event loop
  takes to reschedule a sleeping task. The API runs a single event loop, so
  this delay is paid by *every* concurrent request, including this one.
  Unlike per-request `duration_ms`, it sees work that blocks the loop after
  a response is sent or inside a background job (CH-Api#110).
  `max_lag_ms` under 250 is healthy; over 1000 means requests are queueing.

- **ch_api_profile** (every 6h) - fetches a real company profile and verifies
  the response fields our code depends on are still present and correctly typed.
  Detects silent CH API schema changes before they break customers.

- **rate_limit** (every 1h) - checks the `X-Ratelimit-Remain` header and
  alerts when the budget drops below 20% of the 600-per-5-minutes allowance.

- **document_api** (every 12h) - fetches filing history and hits the CH
  Document API to confirm iXBRL downloads are still accessible.

Possible statuses:
- **pass** - probe succeeded with no issues
- **degraded** - probe completed but detected a warning condition
- **fail** - probe failed (connection error, unexpected HTTP status, missing fields)

**Note:** Results are stored in memory. After a server restart, probes run once
immediately at startup and then on their normal schedule.

No authentication required. Safe to poll at low frequency (once per minute max).

**Upstream usage:** 0 - reads from memory only. No upstream calls made.

200.description: Probe results returned (may be empty if probes haven't run yet)

get.description:
Search for UK companies by name.

Returns a list of matching companies with basic details. Results are cached for 1 hour.

**Example:** `/v1/search?q=tesco` returns Tesco PLC, Tesco Stores Limited, etc.

**With enrichment:** `/v1/search?q=tesco&enrich=true` also includes company age,
accounts status, and size classification for each result (capped at 10 enriched results).

---

**Upstream usage:** 1 upstream call per unique search query (cached for 1 hour).
Repeating the same query within the hour is free - no upstream call is made.
At high volume, you can safely issue ~100 unique searches per minute before
responses begin to slow. Beyond that, requests queue briefly (typically a few seconds)
while upstream capacity recovers.

get.description:
Get an enriched company profile by company number.

Returns the company's core details plus derived fields that aren't available
from the raw Companies House data:

- **company_age_years** - calculated from incorporation date
- **company_category** - inferred size (micro/small/medium/large) based on accounts type
- **accounts.overdue** - whether annual accounts are past their filing deadline
- **confirmation_statement.overdue** - whether the confirmation statement is overdue

Data is cached for 30 days. If the Companies House API is down, stale cached data
is returned with `cached: true` in the response.

**Example:** `/v1/company/00445790` returns the enriched profile for Tesco PLC.

---

**Upstream usage:** 1 upstream call per unique company on first fetch (cached for 30 days).
Repeating a lookup for the same company within 30 days is free - no upstream call is made.
At high volume, you can safely look up ~100 different companies per minute before responses
begin to slow. Beyond that, requests queue briefly (typically a few seconds) while upstream
capacity recovers.

get.summary: Whole company page in one request
get.description:
Fetch the profile, compliance, financials, PSC and directors in one call.

Everything the standalone endpoints return, assembled concurrently and
delivered in a single response. Intended for anything that renders a whole
company at once - a page, a report, a dashboard - where five round trips
cost five authentications and five quota decisions to answer one question.

**Sections are independent.** Each is fetched by the same code that serves
its own endpoint, so plan gating, caching and freshness behave identically.
If one fails, its key is `null` and `section_errors` says why; the rest of
the bundle is unaffected. A caller that requires a section must check for
`null` rather than assume presence.

**The profile is the exception.** It is always included and always fatal: a
company that does not exist returns 404 here, exactly as it does on
`/v1/company/{number}`.

**`section_fetched_at`** carries the per-section `fetched_at` instant. Show a
reader the *oldest* of them - collapsing five timestamps into one overstates
the freshness of whichever section was cached longest.

**Credits:** 1. A bundle costs exactly one call against your quota, however
many sections it carries - which is the point of it.

**Upstream usage:** identical to calling the same sections separately - this
saves our per-request overhead, not Companies House calls.

**Example:** `/v1/company/00445790/bundle?include=profile,financials`

get.summary: Get company directors with their other appointments
get.description:
Get all directors for a company, split into current and past, with their other board appointments.

For each director, the response includes every other company they sit on (or have sat on),
enabling you to map connections between companies through shared board members.

- **current_directors** - officers with no resignation date, including secretaries
  (never filtered - a secretary is a real officer that KYB checks need to see)
- **past_directors** - officers who have resigned
- **other_appointments** - every other company each director is or was appointed to

Each director carries ECCTA identity verification state: **verification_status**
(`verified` | `pending` | `overdue` | `unknown` | `not_applicable`),
**verification_deadline** (this person's own CH-authoritative deadline, only set
when pending or overdue), and **is_board_director** (true for every officer except
secretaries - a `corporate-director` IS a board director even though it cannot
personally verify an identity, so `verification_status` is `not_applicable` for it
while `is_board_director` stays `true`). `pending` means a deadline has been
recorded but has NOT passed - nothing has been missed. Top-level counts
(`directors_verified`, `directors_pending`, `directors_overdue`, `directors_unknown`,
`directors_verification_required`) exclude officers ECCTA does not apply to
(corporate officers and secretaries), so they can be smaller than `total_current`.

Data is cached for 30 days. If the Companies House API is down, stale cached data
is returned with `cached: true` in the response.

**Example:** `/v1/company/00445790/directors` returns all Tesco PLC directors.

---

**Upstream usage:** This endpoint is upstream-intensive on first fetch.
It makes **1 call per director** (to retrieve their appointment history), plus 1–2 calls
for the officer list itself. A company with 10 directors uses ~12 upstream calls;
a company with 50 directors uses ~52. After the first fetch, the result is cached for
30 days and subsequent calls are free.

At high volume, **querying more than ~8 different companies per minute on cold cache**
will cause responses to slow while upstream capacity recovers (typically 5–15 seconds).
For bulk use cases, space requests out or pre-warm the cache during off-peak hours.

get.summary: Map connected companies via shared directors
get.description:
Discover all companies connected to the target through shared board members.

This is the key differentiator of this API: starting from one company, you can see
every other company that shares at least one current director, revealing hidden
governance links and corporate group structures.

- **connections** - each connected company with the list of shared director names
- **connection_strength** - number of shared directors (higher = stronger link)
- **truncated** - `true` if depth=2 traversal hit the 30-company cap (see below)
- Results are sorted by connection strength (strongest first)

Only genuine board directors contribute to connections - corporate secretaries
(e.g. a company secretarial provider shared by thousands of client companies) are
excluded, so a shared corporate-secretary provider never creates a phantom
"connection" between otherwise unrelated companies.

**Depth 1** (default): direct connections only - companies sharing a director with the target.
**Depth 2**: also traverses each connected company's directors to find second-degree connections.
This reveals wider networks but is upstream-intensive on cold cache.

Data is cached for 30 days (cache key includes depth). If the Companies House API is
down, stale cached data is returned with `cached: true`.

**Plan gating:** `depth=2` requires a Pro or Enterprise plan (403 for Free/Web). `depth=1`
is available on all plans.

**Example:** `/v1/company/00445790/network?depth=1` shows companies connected to Tesco PLC.

---

**Upstream usage:** This is the most upstream-intensive endpoint.

- **Depth 1 (cold cache):** same as `/directors` - ~N+2 upstream calls, where N is the number
  of directors. A 10-director company uses ~12 calls; a 50-director company uses ~52 calls.
  After first fetch, cached for 30 days at no cost.

- **Depth 2 (cold cache):** traverses each connected company's directors as well. To protect
  service quality for all customers, traversal is **capped at 30 connected companies** per request.
  Typical upstream cost: 50–200 calls. If the cap is hit, the response includes `truncated: true`
  and `truncated_at: 30` - this means more connections exist but were not explored.

**Practical guidance:** Depth=2 on cold cache is slow by design. On a warm cache (after the
first request), depth=2 is instant and free. If you need depth=2 across many companies,
call `/directors` for each first to warm the cache, then request the network.

At high volume, **querying more than ~8 different companies per minute at depth=1** or
**more than 2–3 different companies per 5 minutes at depth=2** on cold cache will cause
responses to slow while upstream capacity recovers.

get.summary: Get structured financial data from filed accounts
get.description:
Get structured financial data extracted from the company's latest filed iXBRL accounts.

Returns balance sheet and profit & loss figures for the current and prior reporting year,
where available. All monetary values are in actual GBP (e.g. `5200000` = £5,200,000).

**What you get:**

- **profit_and_loss** - turnover, gross profit, operating profit, profit before/after tax,
  depreciation. Only available for companies that file full accounts.
- **balance_sheet** - fixed assets, current assets, creditors, net assets, equity.
  Available for virtually all UK companies (legally mandated).
- **other** - average number of employees during the period.
- **data_quality** - tells you exactly what was extracted, what's missing, and why.
  Use `accounts_type` to understand field availability, and `filing_type` / `filed_on` /
  `period_end_source` to audit *which* Companies House filing the figures came from.

**Which filing is used:** the most recent filing that is genuinely a set of annual accounts
for this company (`AA`, `AAMD`, legacy `AC(NI)`). Companies House files change-of-accounting-
reference-date forms (`AA01`) and similar administrative documents in the same filing-history
category, and they can be filed after the last real accounts - those are skipped.
`data_quality.period_end` is the accounting period end, not the date the filing was
submitted; the submission date is `data_quality.filed_on`.

**Why some fields are null:**

UK law allows smaller companies to withhold P&L data:
- **micro** (`accounts_type: "micro"`) - balance sheet only; turnover and profit are legally
  exempt from disclosure. ~50% of UK companies file micro accounts.
- **abbreviated** (`accounts_type: "abbreviated"`) - balance sheet only; small company
  exemption from P&L disclosure.
- **full** (`accounts_type: "full"`) - all fields available (medium/large companies).

If a field is null, check `data_quality.missing_fields` for the list and
`data_quality.has_profit_loss` to understand whether P&L was filed at all.

**Sources:**

Data is extracted from whichever format is available in the filed accounts:
- **iXBRL** (inline XBRL) - structured markup, high precision, `data_quality.source: "ixbrl"`.
  Covers most UK companies since CH made iXBRL filing mandatory for most company types.
- **PDF** - text/table extraction attempted as a fallback. In practice, PDF annual accounts
  on Companies House are rendered as image-based PDFs (from design software or scanning)
  and yield no extractable text.

If no parseable filing is available (no digital filing, or an image-based PDF) or the
company is dissolved/in liquidation/administration, returns HTTP 200 with `available: false`,
`unavailable_reason` (`"dissolved"`, `"no_ixbrl_filings"` or `"image_pdf"`), `company_status`,
and accounts metadata from the company profile. This lets pipelines branch cleanly without
exception handling. HTTP 404 is only returned when the company number itself does not exist
in Companies House.

Data is cached for 90 days. Financial filings don't change between annual submissions,
so cached data is reliably current.

**Example:** `/v1/company/00445790/financials` returns Tesco PLC's latest filed accounts.

---

**Upstream usage:** 2–3 upstream calls on cold cache (filing history + document metadata +
document download). After first fetch, cached for 90 days at no cost. On cold cache,
limit to ~30 different companies per minute to stay within upstream capacity.

get.description:
Get the PSC (Persons with Significant Control) register for a company.

Returns all active and ceased PSCs, split into categories. `kind` is a closed
enum decided by an explicit allow-list of every Companies House PSC kind:

- **individual** - a natural person with significant control
- **corporate-entity** - a company with significant control
- **legal-person** - a legal person (e.g., government body) with significant control
- **super-secure** - a person whose details are protected by court order
- **unknown** - Companies House returned a kind we have not classified. Nothing
  is inferred from it: no verification status, no chain traversal.

Every PSC also carries **`kind_raw`** - the verbatim Companies House `kind`
string (e.g. `individual-beneficial-owner`). Before 2026-08-01 an
unrecognised kind was echoed into `kind` itself; it is now normalised to
`unknown` and the original value is always available in `kind_raw`.

**Corporate-entity PSCs - which register the number belongs to.** Companies
House stores a corporate PSC's number as the entity's number at whatever
registry `identification.place_registered` names, which is often not
Companies House (Guernsey Registry, Jersey Financial Services Commission,
Commercial Register Of Liechtenstein, ...). Four fields make this explicit:

- `registry_number` - the number exactly as filed, at whatever registry issued it
- `registry_name` - that registry's name as filed
- `registry_is_companies_house` - `true` (confirmed UK register), `null` (a
  number is present but cannot be tied to the UK register), `false` (no
  registration number filed at all)
- `company_number` - populated **only** when `registry_is_companies_house`
  is `true`, and always in canonical Companies House form (zero-padded,
  upper-cased), so it can be passed straight back to this API

Before 2026-08-01 `company_number` carried the raw filed value whatever
register it came from, so a foreign number could zero-pad onto an unrelated
UK company (CH-Api#59). Clients that need the old raw behaviour should read
`registry_number`.

Each PSC includes decoded `natures_of_control_decoded` with human-readable descriptions
of the control type (e.g., "Owns 25-50% of shares" instead of `ownership-of-shares-25-to-50-percent`).

Companies exempt from PSC filing (e.g., listed PLCs on regulated markets) return
`has_psc_exemption: true` with empty PSC lists.

Data is cached for 30 days. If the Companies House API is down, stale cached data
is returned with `cached: true` in the response.

**Example:** `/v1/company/12345678/psc`

---

**Upstream usage:** 1 upstream call per unique company on first fetch (cached for 30 days).
Companies with >100 PSCs require additional pagination calls.

get.summary: Resolve PSC ownership chain to find ultimate beneficial owners
get.description:
Resolve the PSC ownership chain for a company, traversing corporate entity PSCs recursively.

Starting from the given company, fetches its PSCs. When a PSC is a corporate entity
registered at Companies House, follows it to find *that* company's PSCs, and so on,
until reaching natural persons, foreign entities, or the depth limit.

**Terminal reasons** explain why a branch stopped:

- `natural_person` - reached an individual (ultimate beneficial owner)
- `legal_person` - reached a legal person (e.g., government body)
- `super_secure` - person's details protected by court order
- `foreign_entity` - corporate entity with no registration number filed at all
- `unverified_registry` - a registration number is filed, but it cannot be
  tied to the Companies House register (a foreign registry, or a registry
  name we do not recognise). The branch stops rather than following a number
  that may belong to an unrelated UK company. `registry_number` and
  `registry_name` on the node say what was filed.
- `depth_limit` - max traversal depth reached
- `not_found` - company not found or API error
- `cycle_detected` - circular ownership detected
- `psc_exempt` - company exempt from PSC filing (e.g., listed PLC)
- `unknown_kind` - Companies House returned a PSC kind we have not classified.
  The branch stops rather than guessing; `kind_raw` carries the raw value.

**ECCTA identity verification.** Every `individual` node in the tree - at any
depth, including the ultimate beneficial owners the chain exists to find -
carries the same four fields as `/company/{number}/psc`, with the same
meanings:

- `verification_status` - `verified` | `pending` | `overdue` | `unknown`
- `identity_verified` - `true` (verified), `false` (**overdue only**), or
  `null` for pending and unknown. A pending person has missed nothing.
- `identity_verified_on` - set only when `verification_status` is `verified`
- `verification_deadline` - that person's own Companies House deadline, set
  only when `pending` or `overdue`. Companies House's open-ended-window
  sentinel (9999-12-31) is never surfaced; such a person is `pending` with a
  `null` deadline.

Corporate-entity, legal-person, super-secure and unknown nodes omit these
fields entirely - a company has no personal identity to verify, so a status
on one would imply an obligation that does not exist.

Before 2026-08-17 the chain reported no verification data at all, so the same
person could appear verified on `/psc` and blank here (CH-Api#104). Every
person in the tree is classified against a single date fixed at the start of
the traversal.

**Credits:** Each company resolved in the chain costs 1 upstream API call.
The `chain_metadata.total_credits` field shows the total cost.

**Example:** `/v1/company/12345678/psc/chain?max_depth=3`

get.summary: Get ECCTA identity verification compliance snapshot
get.description:
ECCTA identity verification compliance snapshot for a company.

Returns a verification health report for all current directors and active
individual PSCs under the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023.
Mandatory identity verification was introduced in November 2025, with enforcement
beginning 18 November 2026.

**Fields:**

- `directors_total` / `pscs_total` - count of persons ECCTA identity verification
  actually applies to: current (non-resigned) directors minus corporate officers
  and secretaries, and active individual PSCs minus corporate/legal-person PSCs.
  **Not the board size.** It is smaller than `/company/{number}/directors`'
  `total_current`, which counts every current officer including secretaries and
  corporate officers.
- `directors_verified` / `pscs_verified` - count Companies House's public register
  shows as verified: either an `identity_verified_on` date (verified through an
  ACSP) or an open-ended verification window (verified directly with Companies
  House, which publishes no date).
- `directors_pending` / `pscs_pending` - count with a verification deadline that has
  NOT yet passed. Nothing has been missed; during the Nov 2025 - Nov 2026 transition
  this is the majority state for UK directors.
- `directors_overdue` / `pscs_overdue` - count whose deadline has passed with no
  verification recorded.
- `directors_unknown` / `pscs_unknown` - count where `identity_verification_details`
  is entirely absent from the CH API response (pre-ECCTA data, not evidence of
  non-compliance).
- `directors_unverified` / `pscs_unverified` - **deprecated aliases**, kept only for
  backwards compatibility. They now mean exactly `overdue` (CH-Api#52, fixed
  2026-07-30); before that fix they also counted `pending` people, which branded
  roughly 70% of UK directors non-compliant during the transition. Use
  `directors_pending`/`directors_overdue` (or the PSC equivalents) instead.
- `verification_rate` - `verified / (verified + pending + overdue)`, **directors and
  PSCs combined into one figure**. Unknowns are excluded from both the numerator and
  the denominator. `0.0` when nobody is verified, pending or overdue.
- `verification_risk` - `compliant` | `pending` | `partial` | `high_risk` |
  `unknown`. A future deadline is deliberately not treated as risk on its own
  (`pending`); only a passed deadline with no verification drives `high_risk`.
- `risk_score` - `1.0 - verification_rate`, or `null` when no person has a known
  status (verified, pending or overdue) - i.e. everyone is `unknown`.
- `unverified_persons` - every director/PSC who is `pending` **or** `overdue` (both,
  not overdue-only), each carrying its own `status` (`pending` | `overdue`) and
  `deadline`. **Read `status` before describing anyone here as non-compliant** - a
  `pending` entry has missed nothing. `deadline` may be `null` (an open-ended
  verification window with no printable date); never substitute a fallback date for
  a null one. **This list is longer than the `*_unverified` counts by design**: the
  deprecated aliases count `overdue` only, this list carries `pending` too -
  comparing `len(unverified_persons)` to `directors_unverified + pscs_unverified`
  and expecting them to match is the mistake to avoid.
- `eccta_enforcement_deadline` - 2026-11-18

Corporate entity and legal person PSCs are exempt from individual verification and
are excluded from all counts.

**Plan gating:** Pro or Enterprise only. Free and Web plan requests return 403.

**Cache:** 30-day TTL. Officers and PSC are fetched concurrently.

**Credits:** 1 credit per call.

**Example:** `/v1/company/00445790/compliance`

post.description:
Create a webhook subscription to watch UK companies for changes.

Registrum checks each watched company roughly every 15 minutes. When a change
is detected (e.g., status becomes dissolved, accounts go overdue), a signed
POST is delivered to your URL.

**Supported events:**
- `status_change` - company_status changes (e.g., active → dissolved)
- `accounts_overdue` - accounts filing deadline missed
- `confirmation_overdue` - confirmation statement deadline missed
- `directors_changed` - a director is appointed or resigned (checked every 6 hours)
- `pscs_changed` - a PSC is added, ceased, or their ECCTA verification status changes (every 6 hours)
- `compliance_risk_changed` - the company's overall ECCTA risk rating changes, e.g., compliant → partial
  (every 6 hours). **Requires Pro/Enterprise or the Compliance Monitoring add-on.**

**Webhook watch caps** - the number of *distinct* companies you can watch across all
your webhooks (existing + this request combined), by plan:

| Plan | Companies watched |
|------|--------------------|
| Free | 1 |
| Web | 5 |
| Pro | 25 |
| Enterprise | 250 |

Exceeding your cap, or requesting `compliance_risk_changed` without Pro/Enterprise,
returns `403 PLAN_REQUIRED`. The **Compliance Monitoring add-on** raises your cap to
100 companies and unlocks `compliance_risk_changed` on any plan.

**Payload delivered to your URL:**
```json
{
  "event": "company_updated",
  "company_number": "00445790",
  "changes": {
    "status_change": {"from": "active", "to": "dissolved"}
  },
  "triggered_at": "2026-03-11T10:00:00Z"
}
```

**Verifying signatures:**
Every delivery includes an `X-Registrum-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header.
Verify it with HMAC-SHA256 using the `secret` returned at creation time:
```python
import hmac, hashlib
expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), request.body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
assert hmac.compare_digest(expected, request.headers["X-Registrum-Signature"])
```

**Note:** The `secret` is returned once at creation - store it securely.

200.description: Webhook created. Response includes the signing secret - store it securely.

400.description: Invalid event type or company number

403.description: Plan required: either the request would exceed your plan's webhook watch cap, or compliance_risk_changed was requested without Pro/Enterprise or the Compliance Monitoring add-on.

get.description:
Get a comprehensive Know Your Business (KYB) report for a UK company.

Aggregates the company profile, financial data, director information, and a computed
set of risk flags into a single response. Suitable for onboarding, due diligence,
and automated KYB workflows.

**Report sections:**

- **profile** - enriched company profile (status, age, address, SIC codes)
- **financials** - latest filed accounts (balance sheet + P&L). `null` if no digital filing exists.
- **directors** - current and past directors with their other appointments
- **psc_chain** - PSC ownership chain resolved to ultimate beneficial owners. Each node has a
  `terminal_reason` (natural_person, foreign_entity, legal_person, psc_exempt, depth_limit,
  not_found, cycle_detected). `null` if chain resolution fails.
- **compliance** - ECCTA identity-verification snapshot for the directors and individual
  PSCs the regime actually applies to, identical to `/v1/company/{number}/compliance`.
  **Read `status` before calling anyone non-compliant**: `pending` means the deadline has
  not arrived yet and nothing has been missed, which is the majority state for UK
  directors during the Nov 2025 - Nov 2026 transition. Only `overdue` is a missed
  deadline. `null` for Free and Web plans, which the compliance endpoint does not cover.
- **risk_flags** - boolean flags derived from the profile and filing data:
  - `accounts_overdue` - accounts past their filing deadline
  - `confirmation_overdue` - confirmation statement overdue
  - `has_charges` - company has registered charges (e.g., mortgages)
  - `has_insolvency_history` - any insolvency history on record
  - `not_active` - company is not in active status (dissolved, liquidation, etc.)
  - `recently_incorporated` - less than 1 year old
  - `financials_unavailable` - no parseable digital accounts filing exists
  - `no_accounts_type` - no accounts type recorded (dormant or never filed)
- **summary_md** - LLM-ready Markdown combining profile + financials summaries

**Credits:** 1. A KYB report costs exactly one call against your quota, however many
sections it carries. `psc_chain.chain_metadata.total_credits` counts companies resolved
in the ownership chain, which is a measure of chain depth, not of quota spent.

**Cache behaviour:** All underlying data sources are served from cache where available.
Profile: 30-day TTL. Financials: 90-day TTL. Directors: 30-day TTL. PSC: fetched fresh per call.

**Example:** `/v1/company/00445790/kyb-report` returns a full KYB report for Tesco PLC.

post.summary: Submit a batch of up to 500 companies for async enrichment
post.description:
Submit a list of up to 500 UK company numbers for background enrichment.

Unlike `POST /v1/enrich` (which processes up to 50 companies synchronously),
this endpoint accepts much larger lists and processes them in the background,
automatically respecting the shared Companies House API rate limit.

**How it works:**
1. Submit your list - receive a `batch_id` immediately.
2. Poll `GET /v1/batch/{batch_id}` every few seconds until `status` is terminal.
3. Read `results` for successful enrichments and `errors` for any failures.

**Status lifecycle:**
```
queued → processing → complete
                   ↘ partial          (some successes, some errors)
                   ↘ failed           (all companies errored)
                   ↘ quota_exceeded   (monthly credit limit hit mid-batch)
```

**Credits:**
1 credit is charged per company successfully processed (or attempted).
Credits are deducted as processing proceeds, not upfront.
Polling `GET /v1/batch/{batch_id}` is always free.

**Expiry:**
Job results are kept for 7 days after creation and then automatically deleted.

**Example request:**
```json
POST /v1/batch
{"company_numbers": ["00445790", "03547512", "SC123456"]}
```

**Example immediate response:**
```json
{
  "batch_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
  "status": "queued",
  "total_companies": 3,
  "estimated_wait_seconds": 10
}
```

**Poll until complete:**
```
GET /v1/batch/3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6
```

400.description: Empty list or list exceeds 500 companies

accounts_type.title: Accounts Type
accounts_type.description: Type of accounts filed: 'full', 'abbreviated', 'micro', 'dormant', or 'unknown'. Micro and abbreviated accounts legally exclude P&L - turnover and profit fields will be null. This is expected, not a data error. Changed 2026-08-01 (CH-Api#61): this was previously derived by keyword-matching Companies House's machine-readable filing code against a list of English prose phrases, and anything unmatched defaulted to 'full'. About 17% of filers were mis-typed - most commonly `unaudited-abridged`, which is now correctly 'abbreviated'. Values that were already right are unchanged. See `accounts_description_code` for the verbatim Companies House code and `accounts_type_source` for how this value was resolved.

accounts_type_source.title: Accounts Type Source
accounts_type_source.description: How `accounts_type` was determined: 'ch_filing_description' (read from the Companies House filing code - the normal case), 'xbrl_namespace' (inferred from the accounting taxonomy declared inside the document, e.g. FRS-105 = micro), 'pl_presence_inference' (the filing carries no type but the document plainly contains a profit and loss account), or 'unresolved' (nothing identified it; `accounts_type` is 'unknown' and scoring falls back to the balance sheet only).

accounts_description_code.title: Accounts Description Code
accounts_description_code.description: The verbatim Companies House accounts-type code from the filing description, e.g. 'total-exemption-full', 'unaudited-abridged', 'micro-entity'. Null when the filing description carries no accounts type at all (`accounts-with-made-up-date`). Exposed so you can apply your own classification rather than trusting ours.

completeness.title: Completeness
completeness.description: Fraction of expected fields successfully extracted (0.0–1.0). The denominator is set per accounts_type: 20 fields for 'full', 13 for 'abbreviated', 5 for 'micro', 4 for 'dormant', and 12 (balance sheet only) for 'unknown'. A score of 0.85 on full accounts is normal. Note this score generally ROSE on 2026-08-01 for abridged and small-company filers (CH-Api#61): they had been scored against a profit and loss account they are legally forbidden to file.

fields_attempted.title: Fields Attempted
fields_attempted.description: Number of fields expected for this accounts_type - the denominator of `completeness`. 20 for 'full', 13 for 'abbreviated', 5 for 'micro', 4 for 'dormant', 12 for 'unknown'.

fields_extracted.title: Fields Extracted
fields_extracted.description: Number of fields successfully extracted from the filing.

has_profit_loss.title: Has Profit Loss
has_profit_loss.description: Whether P&L data (turnover, profit, etc.) was found in the filing. False for micro-entities and abbreviated accounts - this is legal, not an error.

has_balance_sheet.title: Has Balance Sheet
has_balance_sheet.description: Whether balance sheet data was found. Should be True for all UK companies.

missing_fields.title: Missing Fields
missing_fields.description: List of field names that are null in this response. For full accounts, this may include optional fields not filed. For micro/abbreviated accounts, this will include all P&L fields.

field_confidence.title: Field Confidence
field_confidence.description: Per-field confidence score (0.0–1.0) for PDF-extracted data. Empty for iXBRL (iXBRL extraction is deterministic - implicit 1.0). Use this to filter out low-confidence PDF extractions. Scores below 0.70 indicate a broad/fuzzy label match.

period_end.title: Period End
period_end.description: Accounting period end date (YYYY-MM-DD) - the date the accounts are made up to. Until 2026-08-01 (CH-Api#60) this was the date the filing was submitted to Companies House, which is a different and later date (commonly by months). It is now taken from the filing's `made_up_date`, or from the document's own reporting contexts. See `period_end_source` for which. The submission date is still available, unchanged, as `filed_on`.

period_end_source.title: Period End Source
period_end_source.description: Where `period_end` came from, so you can audit it: 'description_values.made_up_date' (the Companies House filing's own made-up-to date - the normal case), 'document_context' (the reporting period declared inside the filed document itself), 'description_values.action_date', or 'filing_date' (a legacy paper filing that carries no period metadata - treat with caution).

filed_on.title: Filed On
filed_on.description: The date the selected filing was submitted to Companies House (YYYY-MM-DD). Distinct from `period_end`: accounts for a period ending 31 December are typically filed the following year.

filing_type.title: Filing Type
filing_type.description: The Companies House form code of the filing these figures were extracted from: 'AA' (annual accounts), 'AAMD' (amended accounts) or 'AC(NI)' (legacy Northern Irish accounts). Administrative forms in the same filing-history category - 'AA01' change of accounting reference date and friends - are never selected (CH-Api#60).

identity_verified.title: Identity Verified
identity_verified.description: ECCTA identity verification status, collapsed to a tri-state boolean for convenience. True = verified with Companies House (a confirmed identity_verified_on date exists). False = genuinely overdue - Companies House recorded a deadline that HAS passed with no verification. Before CH-Api#52 this also covered pending people (a future deadline), which wrongly branded ~70% of live officers as unverified; it no longer does. None covers every other case - pending (a deadline recorded but not yet due), unknown (no verification data on record at all), or not_applicable (this officer is outside ECCTA verification, e.g. a corporate officer or secretary). See verification_status to distinguish those three.

identity_verified_on.description: Date identity verification was completed, as recorded by Companies House. Only set when identity_verified is True.

verification_status.title: Verification Status
verification_status.description: The full ECCTA verification state: 'verified' (identity_verified_on present), 'pending' (Companies House recorded a deadline or verification window that has NOT passed - nothing has been missed, this person owes nothing yet), 'overdue' (a recorded deadline has passed with no verification), 'unknown' (no verification data on record at all - not evidence of non-compliance, just absence of data), or 'not_applicable' (this officer is outside ECCTA identity verification entirely - a corporate officer, which has no personal identity to verify, or a secretary, who is not in scope of the regime).

verification_deadline.title: Verification Deadline
verification_deadline.description: This person's own verification deadline as recorded by Companies House - authoritative and per-person, not a company-wide date. Set only when verification_status is 'pending' or 'overdue'. Companies House writes 9999-12-31 internally to mean an open-ended verification window; that sentinel is never surfaced here - an open-ended window returns null rather than a fake calendar date a chase email could quote.

is_board_director.title: Is Board Director
is_board_director.description: True if this officer is a genuine board director (governance role), False only for secretaries. Distinct from ECCTA scope: a corporate director (a company acting as director) IS a board director (is_board_director: true) even though it cannot personally verify an identity (verification_status: not_applicable). Secretaries remain in current_directors/past_directors - this field controls only who counts toward the verification totals and who contributes to /network connections, not who appears in the officer list.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Find UK companies by name. Supports fuzzy matching and pagination. Results are cached for 1 hour.

tags.name: Company
tags.description: Get enriched company profiles by company number. Profiles include derived fields like company age, size classification, and accounts overdue status. Data is cached for 30 days.

tags.name: Directors
tags.description: Discover company directors and map corporate networks through shared board members. Each director includes their other appointments, enabling you to trace governance links between companies. Data is cached for 30 days.

tags.name: Financials
tags.description: Structured financial data extracted from filed iXBRL accounts. Returns balance sheet and P&L figures (where available) for current and prior year. All values in actual GBP. Data is cached for 90 days.

tags.name: PSC
tags.description: Persons with Significant Control (PSC) register. Returns individuals, corporate entities, and legal persons who hold significant control over a company. Includes decoded control types and exemption detection for listed PLCs. Data is cached for 30 days.

tags.name: Compliance
tags.description: ECCTA identity verification compliance snapshots under the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023. Returns a verification health report for all current directors and active individual PSCs - who's verified, who isn't, and an overall risk rating. Pro and Enterprise plan only. Cached for 30 days.

tags.name: KYB
tags.description: Know Your Business report. Aggregates company profile, financials, directors, and computed risk flags into a single endpoint. Suitable for onboarding, due diligence, and automated compliance workflows.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Subscribe to company change events. Registrum polls watched companies every 15 minutes and delivers a signed POST to your URL when a status, accounts, or confirmation-statement change is detected. Deliveries are signed with HMAC-SHA256. Distinct companies watched are capped by plan (free=1, web=5, pro=25, enterprise=250); the Compliance Monitoring add-on raises the cap to 100 and unlocks the compliance_risk_changed event on any plan.

tags.name: Enrich
tags.description: Bulk enrichment endpoint. Enrich up to 50 UK companies in a single POST request. Each company is looked up in parallel with a cache-first strategy. Partial success is supported - individual items can fail without failing the whole batch.

tags.name: Batch
tags.description: Async batch enrichment. Submit a list of up to 500 UK company numbers and Registrum enriches them in the background, automatically managing the Companies House API rate limit. Poll `GET /v1/batch/{batch_id}` for progress - polling is always free. Results are retained for 7 days. Ideal for bulk data pipelines and list processing.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Service health checks. These endpoints do **not** require authentication and are safe to use for uptime monitoring.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Check your API key's usage and quota. `GET /v1/usage` is free - it does not consume a credit.

tags.name: Feedback
tags.description: Submit bug reports or feature requests directly from your integration. Feedback is reviewed by the Registrum team and helps prioritise fixes and improvements. Authenticated with your API key - no extra setup required.
